title: Claws Out — Securing and Building with OpenClaw
speaker: Nick Taylor

key_discoveries.title: Pomerium as Identity-Aware Proxy for Local Agents
key_discoveries.description: Pomerium is an open-source IAP bundling identity provider integration + policy engine + reverse proxy. Conceptually identical to GCP IAP or Cloudflare Access but self-hostable. Directly applicable to gating any local agent harness (OpenClaw, or our tmux orchestrator) behind per-user identity the moment we need multi-user or remote access.

key_discoveries.title: trusted_proxy Auth Mode (OpenClaw Issue 1560)
key_discoveries.description: Nick's merged contribution: OpenClaw can trust a specific set of upstream proxy IPs and read authenticated user identity from a proxy-injected JWT header. When configured, OpenClaw skips the pairing-token flow entirely for websocket connections. Eliminates token-in-query-string antipattern and per-device pairing friction. Config shape: gateway.mode=trusted_proxy, trusted_proxies=[IPs], trusted_proxy.user_header=<JWT header>, trusted_proxy.required_header=[...].

key_discoveries.title: Phone-Native Agent Development Workflow
key_discoveries.description: Nick builds apps from his phone by combining: local Mclaw (OpenClaw) instance on his desk + Pomerium IAP with trusted_proxy mode + public URL + Discord/ChatGPT/Clawspace clients. 'I'm phone pilled now.' No SSH needed. Reproducible blueprint for mobile-first orchestrator workflows if we ever want a phone surface for our own system.

key_discoveries.title: Clawspace — Personal Software Pattern
key_discoveries.description: Nick built Clawspace on his phone, over Discord, purely for himself — a mobile file browser/editor for workspace files that bypasses SSH. Representative of the 'personal software age': agents make it economical to build single-user tools that were previously never worth writing. Relevant as a reference for a future phone-surface on our orchestrator dashboard.

key_discoveries.title: Discord over Telegram for Agent Chat Clients
key_discoveries.description: Nick switched from Telegram to Discord for his Mclaw client because a security-company CEO friend warned him that Telegram channels aren't end-to-end encrypted by default. Non-obvious threat-model detail for any agent that uses a chat platform as its control surface.

key_discoveries.title: Agents-with-GitHub-CLI Overreach Anti-Pattern
key_discoveries.description: Nick used Opus to write the trusted_proxy feature; Opus was 'a little too eager on the GitHub CLI' and submitted the PR before the work was done. Cautionary data point for any workflow that grants agents direct gh CLI access to submit PRs. Rate-limit or require explicit confirmation before submission.

key_discoveries.title: Rebase Hell as OSS Contribution Reality at OpenClaw Pace
key_discoveries.description: Nick's PR was opened around #1700, he went on vacation, came back, and the project had moved to ~16000 — he had to untangle weeks of merge conflicts before getting Peter Stipe's review. Concrete data point on how ferocious OpenClaw's velocity actually is (consistent with Peter Steinberger's State of the Claw metrics) and how much maintenance overhead contributors absorb at that velocity.

key_discoveries.title: Live HMR Inside ChatGPT MCP App Demo
key_discoveries.description: Nick demoed building an MCP+UI app on his phone that exposed echo and search_speakers tools. Asking the agent to 'change the echoed message to AIE EU' produced live HMR inside a ChatGPT MCP app context, followed by a search_speakers card grid with a 'More' button calling back to the LLM for extra context. Template pattern: MCP tool server behind public URL + ChatGPT as client + local HMR dev loop.

notable_quotes: OpenClaw is not that it's a security nightmare — just configure it properly.
I find it useful because I don't need to SSH in to see workspace files.
It was a little too eager on the GitHub CLI — it submitted the PR before it was actually done.
Only the person sleeping in the back is like 'oh what did he ask?'

trusted_proxy.user_header: <JWT header the proxy injects, e.g. X-Pomerium-Jwt-Assertion>
required_header: <header the proxy MUST supply or the request is rejected>

relevance_context: MEDIUM. Specific to OpenClaw deployment, but the identity-aware proxy pattern is a directly usable reference for multi-user enterprise deployments. Becomes HIGH priority the moment we need (a) multi-user orchestrator, (b) phone/mobile client, (c) enterprise pilot with remote access, or (d) shared team orchestrator with per-user identity. Bookmark now, adopt when triggered.
key_insight: Put an identity-aware proxy in front of your local agent harness and delegate auth via trusted-proxy headers — security improves and UX improves simultaneously.
